_comment: Launch mechanics per adapter, machine-readable so scripts/leg-cmd.sh can
emit an exact command and scripts/lint.py can hold the prose to it.
Why this file exists: every launch fact in it was already documented in
some SKILL.md or references/*-runtime.md, and leads kept composing launch
commands from memory anyway -- measured 2026-09-08, five wrong launches in
one session, every one of them contradicted by a line already in the repo.
Another paragraph telling the lead to read the runtime file does not fix
that; the lead had already been told, in each leg's opening section.
So: the command comes out of a script, not out of recall.
Like data/families.json this file DECLARES. It generates no documentation.
The lint rule only checks that the prose does not CONTRADICT it.
effort.mechanism is the field that keeps being got wrong, because all four
model_suffix -- the effort is part of the model string (agy, cursor)
config_only  -- no per-call control at all (codex review path)
none         -- the adapter has no effort concept (claude)

2026-09-08 second pass: a four-leg review found this file disagreed with the repo's own skills in almost every role its author had NOT personally probed -- an invented agy timeout, an agy implement launch with no write mode, an invented cursor --force with --trust dropped, grok missing the three flags that ARE its read-only boundary, claude missing the MCP trim and with the wrong prompt delivery. Every one was transcription from recall, which is the exact failure this file exists to stop, one level up. Hence per-ROLE verified strings: believe the review rows, re-check an implement row against its skill before trusting it.

implement.verified: transcribed from the matching skill; not probed

effort.note: A bare tier name is REJECTED: `--model gemini-3.8-flash` errors with `requires --effort (available: low, medium, high)`. `--model gemini-3.8-flash --effort medium` also works, but the suffixed form is self-contained and cannot disagree with a flag. Verified 2026-09-08 by running all three spellings.

gotchas: `--disable-slash-commands` makes `--mode plan` a no-op -- the CLI warns `--mode plan has no effect while slash command expansion is disabled`. Pick one; for a review leg keep plan mode.
`--add-dir` is mandatory: the headless workspace root is agy's own scratch dir, not your cwd.
The review role DROPS --disable-slash-commands (it makes --mode plan a no-op); the implement role KEEPS it. Do not carry one role's flag set to the other.

implement.verified: 2026-09-13 probed live -- --write and --fresh were missing; without --write codex-companion.mjs runs the session read-only (sandbox: request.write ? workspace-write : read-only), so the mandated dispatch path produced a paid delegate that could not edit

effort.note: The review path has NO effort flag. Source of truth: codex-companion.mjs `handleReviewCommand` parses valueOptions ["base","scope","model","cwd"]; only `handleTask` parses `effort`. So a review leg's depth is whatever the config file says at launch time -- read it and report the value, do not assert one. To make it explicit instead of inherited, bypass the companion with `codex exec -c model_reasoning_effort=<x>`, at the cost of the companion's job tracking and read-only sandbox. Verified 2026-09-08 by reading the script.

gotchas: `--help` is not a flag on `adversarial-review`; it is parsed as focus text and runs a real, billed review. Read the script's usage line instead.
Omitting `--base` reviews the working tree, which is clean right after a commit -- it will report nothing to review.

implement.verified: transcribed from the matching skill; not probed

effort.note: Effort is part of the model id; there is no effort flag. Two separate quota pools: the grok tier has low/medium/high/xhigh (each with a `-fast` twin), while `kimi-k3` has only low/high/max -- there is NO kimi medium. Verified 2026-09-08 via `cursor-agent models`.

gotchas: `--mode ask` is the only posture that both refuses writes and returns a report; bare `-p` writes files, `--mode plan` returns empty output headless.
The pinned model decides the family for cross-family accounting; `auto` and `composer-*` satisfy nothing.
Bare -p IS the write posture; --force/--yolo/--approve-mcps are forbidden on both roles. --trust is required -- without it a fresh worktree prints the trust prompt and exits 0.

implement.verified: transcribed from the matching skill; not probed

effort.note: Values are the provider's, not a fixed set. There is NO reasoningEffort key in opencode.json -- a lead who looks for one silently gets the provider default. `--help` lists `--variant` but it sits below the point a truncated read stops at; that is exactly how it was missed on 2026-09-08. Measured the same day: on an identical brief and frozen commit, xhigh returned 10 findings against the default's 8, including the round's only remote crash.

gotchas: The prompt goes on STDIN. An argv prompt over ~1-2 KB hangs before the session is created.
`tokens.output=0` is a broken counter, not an empty run -- grep the log for your required section headers before discarding it.

review.verified: transcribed from the matching skill; not probed

effort.note: Accepts none..max in principle, but the levels are per-model menus and which ones grok-4.6 advertises is UNVERIFIED. Confirm against the model before relying on a specific level.

gotchas: `--no-memory` on every delegate run: this CLI has cross-session memory and a reviewer that remembers last session's premises is contaminated.

--tools + --disallowed-tools Agent + --deny 'MCPTool(*)' ARE the review boundary, not decoration: ~/.grok/config.toml may be permission_mode = always-approve, and --sandbox alone is a no-op on old kernels.

gotchas: Never the cross-family reviewer for Claude-written work.
Without --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}' the delegate loads the full MCP stack and the startup silence reads as a hang.
